name: Micro Repetition
description: Analyzes the text for abnormal, tight-knit recycling of specific syntactic structures, modifier phrases, or vocabulary within a very short word span. While human writers often catch and edit out awkward, immediate repetition, AI models frequently fall into localized autoregressive loops, reusing the same word or exact phrase several times within just a few sentences.
algorithm: Localized N-Gram Frequency and Autoregressive Loop Detection
mechanism: This algorithm scans the text using a sliding window approach (e.g., 50 to 100 words), searching for 'micro-repetitions'. AI models generate text token by token based on statistical probability. When a specific token or short N-gram is selected, its probability of being selected again in the immediate vicinity often artificially spikes because it enters the model's short-term context window. This phenomenon leads to 'autoregressive loops' where the AI unintentionally echoes its own recent output (e.g., using the word 'crucial' three times in a single paragraph, or starting two consecutive sentences with 'It is important to note'). The system identifies exact string matching, lemma repetition (e.g., 'decide', 'decisions', 'deciding'), and structural echoing within these tight windows. Human writers typically possess an innate stylistic aversion to immediate, unintended repetition and will organically rely on synonyms, pronouns, or sentence restructuring. A high density of micro-repetitions suggests a lack of conscious editorial oversight characteristic of machine generation.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing student essays, automated blog posts, and generated creative writing, where the AI lacks the 'stylistic memory' to realize it just used a specific phrasing seconds ago.
strengths:
• Detects a fundamental flaw in autoregressive generation that is very difficult for current LLMs to suppress without human editing.
• Operates strictly on the text's internal logic, requiring no external reference models or connectivity.
• Highly sensitive to 'lazy' generation where the AI pads out word counts by subtly recycling its own previous clauses.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in texts that demand deliberate repetition for rhetorical effect (e.g., political speeches, poetry) or extreme technical clarity (e.g., medical dosage instructions).
• Less effective on heavily edited AI text, as humans naturally prune these awkward repetitions during review.
• Short texts may lack the necessary volume to establish a statistically significant pattern of repetition.
parameters:
Analysis: Sliding Window N-Gram and Lemma Tracking
Metric: Frequency and Distance of Lexical/Structural Echoes
Output: 0-100 Localized Repetition (Autoregressive Echo) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 76-83% accuracy. It is a highly specific indicator of 'raw', unedited AI output, though it loses efficacy if the text has been manually polished.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
